links.outcome: Safety metrics of expert-edited LLM drafts versus expert-written and unedited LLM responses
links.effect: Expert-edited drafts (Expert + AI) had higher quality and empathy than Expert alone, but were worse than Expert on most safety metrics; e.g. incorrect content low risk 0.801 vs 0.832, with 2% high-risk vs 0%.
links.quote: In terms of safety metrics, utilizing the established methodology from Singhal et al 17 allows for comparisons, where Expert + AI performed worse than Expert in all metrics except missing content.

links.outcome: Whether expert editing of LLM drafts removed incorrect content and potential harm
links.effect: Expert-edited LLM responses retained some inappropriate content and harm potential (2% high-risk incorrect content; 2% high-risk extent of harm); authors note experts may skim and miss errors in drafts.
links.quote: While our timing analysis shows improvement with Expert + AI responses versus Expert responses, Experts may quickly skim and miss content errors in the draft response, thus leading to both time savings and decreased safety metrics.

links.outcome: Quality, empathy, safety and time of experts with AI draft versus experts without AI
links.effect: Expert + AI beat Expert on quality and empathy (both P < 0.001) and saved time (185 vs 289 s, P = 0.02) but had worse safety metrics except missing content; simulated setting, no overreliance assessment.
links.quote: For both quality (P < 0.001) and empathy (P < 0.001), expert-edited LLM responses performed better than expert-created responses.

links.outcome: LLM responses compared against expert-written responses on quality, empathy, safety
links.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 scored higher than Expert in quality (P < 0.001); ChatGPT-4 was similar to Expert on safety metrics, and better on missing content (P = 0.001).
links.quote: Comparing the top LLM (ChatGPT-4) versus Expert demonstrates that the LLM performed similarly (inappropriate and/or incorrect content P = 0.35; extent of possible harm P = 0.356; likelihood of possible harm P = 0.129); or better missing content ( P = 0.001) ( Table 8 ).

links.outcome: Empathy ratings of LLM and expert-edited LLM responses versus expert responses
links.effect: Expert + AI empathy 3.73 vs Expert 2.88 (P < 0.001); ChatGPT-3.5 3.75; several LLMs significantly more empathetic than Expert.
links.quote: In terms of empathy, ChatGPT-4, Bard, Claude, and ChatGPT-3.5 all performed significantly better than Expert.

links.outcome: Clinical knowledge errors and missing content in LLM answers to retina questions
links.effect: LLMs produced incorrect or missing content, e.g. a generalized 3-month anti-VEGF interval and calling retinal vein occlusion an 'eye stroke'; Bard and Bing had the highest proportion of high-risk responses.
links.quote: An LLM suggested a generalized 3-month interval between anti-VEGF injections for most patients, disregarding individual patient needs.

links.outcome: Accuracy and safety assessed against expert graders across response types
links.effect: Expert panel grading of incorrect content, missing content, harm extent and likelihood differed across response types (all P < 0.01); no ground truth for quality and empathy.
links.quote: The study was limited by the subjective nature of quality and empathy outcomes, a judgment without proven ground truth.

links.quote: Furthermore, multiple LLMs performed significantly better in terms of quality (ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4) and empathy (ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5, Bard, and Claude) than human experts.

links.effect: Expert+AI quality 3.86 vs Expert 3.23; empathy 3.73 vs 2.88; low-risk harm 0.859 vs 0.978; missing 0.839 vs 0.642.
links.quote: In terms of safety metrics, utilizing the established methodology from Singhal et al 17 allows for comparisons, where Expert + AI performed worse than Expert in all metrics except missing content.

links.effect: High-risk inappropriate/incorrect content: GPT-4 0.021, GPT-3.5 0.059, Claude 0.080, Bing 0.100, Bard 0.160; Bard high likelihood of harm 0.122.
links.quote: An LLM suggested a generalized 3-month interval between anti-VEGF injections for most patients, disregarding individual patient needs.

links.effect: Mean empathy: GPT-3.5 3.75, Expert+AI 3.73, GPT-4 3.64, Bard 3.36, Claude 3.25, Expert 2.88, Bing 2.61.
links.quote: There were significant differences in both quality (Friedman’s test, P < 0.001) and empathy scores (Friedman’s test, P < 0.001) across the response types.

links.outcome: Incorrect, missing, or harmful clinical content
links.effect: High-risk ranges: incorrect 0.000–0.160, missing 0.000–0.160, extent 0.000–0.121, likelihood 0.000–0.122; all metrics P < 0.01.
links.quote: In terms of safety metrics, there were statistically significant differences between response types for inappropriate and/or incorrect content ( P < 0.01), missing content ( P < 0.01), extent of possible harm ( P < 0.01) and likelihood of possible harm ( P < 0.01) ( Table 8 ).
